newsitem.title: UK: IBCA affirms Bank Austria ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA affirms Bank Austria ratings.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Thursday it had affirmed Bank Austria's A1 plus short-term and AA long-term ratings.
This affirmation followed the bank's announcement to bid for the Austrian government's stake in Creditanstalt Bankverein (Creditanstalt), IBCA said in a statement.
It said, if successful, the bid would give Bank Austria, the country's largest bank, 70 percent of the voting control in Creditanstalt, the country's second largest bank.

"The purchase would be positive for Creditanstalt's short- and long-term ratings of A1 and A plus respectively, if it were to become a subsidiary of Bank Austria," IBCA said. "The purchase also opens the possibility of a subsequent merger of Creditanstalt into Bank Austria."

IBCA said it's affirmation of Bank Austria's ratings are based on the understanding that, following a possible merger, the merged entity would continue to benefit from the deficiency guarantee of the City of Vienna.

"A full takeover of Creditanstalt by Bank Austria, would create by a substantial margin Austria's largest bank, with combined total assets of some $130 billion and domestic market shares of between 20 to 25 percent in most business areas," the rating agency said.

"The merger seems logical from an industry-wide perspective given the overcapacity in the Austrian banking market. However, there have been discussions about the possible purchase of Creditanstalt for the past five years and it remains to be seen whether this attempt will be successful," IBCA said.
